newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close lower despite Band B bids.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close lower despite Band B bids.

text.p: Brazilian stocks seesawed to end lower for a second session in a row despite today's announcement of the names of qualified bidders for the closely watched Band B cellular sell-off, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most active shares closed off 0.72 percent at 11,030 points. Volume was high at 856.1 million reais ($807.6 million).

Even the announcement of the first winning group failed to boost market prices. A Canadian-led consortium won a concession to operate cellular services in central and western Brazil with a bid of 338.5 million reais, some 25.4 percent above the base price.

Traders said the result was positive, but everybody is waiting for the bids presented by the consortia to run the wealthiest areas, comprising Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro states. Also, some said optimism over the Band B cellular privatizations has apparently been priced in, particularly in Telebras stock.

Analysts also said they welcomed Telebras' earnings for the January-to-April period, but the results also failed to bolster the market's opening rise. The firm posted a preliminary net consolidated profit of 965 million reais.
Traders said the market may continue losing ground in coming sessions, especially as speculation ahead of the June 16 options settlement is likely to intensify.
Telebras closed off 1.11 percent at 142.80 reais. State oil firm Petrobras fell 0.4 percent, ending at 246 reais, despite a lower house committe approval of an oil deregulation bill.
Voting shares of Sao Paulo state sewage company Sabesp closed at 290.01 reais in its first day of trade on the stock exchange. Eighty trades were seen in the stock, totalling 7.313 million reais.
The stock had traded on Rio de Janeiro's SOMA over-the-counter market since November.
